objects.description: Core JSON node type representing values (null, boolean, number, string, array, object, or raw). Nodes can be linked in doubly-linked lists via next/prev and form trees via child for arrays/objects. Fields are public; type determines active value fields. Managed and freed via cJSON API (e.g., cJSON_Delete).
Allocator hook table to override memory management used by cJSON. Provide malloc_fn and free_fn (compatible with CDECL on Windows) via cJSON_InitHooks before using the library.
Boolean typedef used by the cJSON API. Semantics: 0 is false, non-zero is true. It is an alias of int; no special construction required.

functions.name: cJSON_Version
functions.description: Returns the cJSON library version string (major.minor.patch). Intended for runtime/version checks or logging.
requirements: No arguments.
Return is a NUL-terminated static string; caller must not free or modify it.

functions.name: cJSON_InitHooks
functions.description: Sets custom memory allocation hooks (malloc and free) to be used by cJSON. Pass NULL or zeroed hooks to reset to defaults.
requirements: hooks may be NULL to reset to defaults.
If hooks is non-NULL and provides malloc_fn or free_fn, they must be compatible with standard malloc/free semantics and calling convention (CDECL on Windows).
Must be called before other cJSON allocation calls to affect them.
Hooks remain in effect globally for subsequent cJSON allocations.

functions.name: cJSON_Parse
functions.description: Parses a NUL-terminated JSON text buffer into a cJSON DOM tree.
requirements: value must point to a NUL-terminated UTF-8/ASCII JSON text buffer.
On success, caller owns the returned cJSON* and must free it with cJSON_Delete.
On failure, returns NULL; use cJSON_GetErrorPtr to locate the parse error.
Input nesting must not exceed CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT; circular reference length must not exceed CJSON_CIRCULAR_LIMIT.

functions.name: cJSON_ParseWithLength
functions.description: Parses JSON from a buffer of given length (not required to be NUL-terminated).
requirements: value must point to a readable buffer of length buffer_length.
buffer_length specifies exact readable length; parsing may stop before end if JSON ends earlier.
On success, free result with cJSON_Delete; on failure, returns NULL and cJSON_GetErrorPtr indicates error.
Subject to CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT and CJSON_CIRCULAR_LIMIT.

functions.name: cJSON_ParseWithOpts
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_ParseWithOpts(const char *value, const char **return_parse_end, cJSON_bool require_null_terminated)
functions.description: Parses a NUL-terminated JSON buffer with options to require full consumption and to return the end pointer.
requirements: value must be a readable NUL-terminated buffer.
If return_parse_end is non-NULL, on success it receives a pointer to the char after the parsed JSON; on failure it receives the error position (same as cJSON_GetErrorPtr).
If require_null_terminated is non-zero, parsing fails unless the parsed JSON ends exactly at the terminating NUL.
On success, caller must free result with cJSON_Delete; returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(const char *value, size_t buffer_length, const char **return_parse_end, cJSON_bool require_null_terminated)
functions.description: Parses JSON from a buffer with explicit length, optionally returning the end position and optionally requiring a trailing NUL after the parsed JSON.
requirements: value must point to a readable buffer of at least buffer_length bytes.
If return_parse_end is non-NULL, it is set as in cJSON_ParseWithOpts (points to error on failure).
If require_null_terminated is non-zero, parsing fails unless the next character after the parsed JSON is '\0'.
On success, free the returned root with cJSON_Delete; returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_Print
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree to a newly allocated formatted (pretty-printed) JSON string.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON tree.
Returns a heap-allocated NUL-terminated string on success; caller must free it using the standard free, the hook free_fn, or cJSON_free consistent with current hooks.
Returns NULL on allocation or encoding failure.

functions.name: cJSON_PrintUnformatted
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree to a newly allocated compact (no extra whitespace) JSON string.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON tree.
Caller must free the returned buffer with standard free/hook free_fn/cJSON_free as appropriate.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_PrintBuffered
functions.signature: char * cJSON_PrintBuffered(const cJSON *item, int prebuffer, cJSON_bool fmt)
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree using an internal buffered strategy; optionally pretty-prints.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON tree.
prebuffer is a size hint (bytes) for initial allocation; must be non-negative.
fmt==0 for unformatted, non-zero for formatted output.
Caller must free returned buffer via the active free routine; returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_PrintPreallocated
functions.signature: cJSON_bool cJSON_PrintPreallocated(cJSON *item, char *buffer, const int length, const cJSON_bool format)
functions.description: Serializes a cJSON tree into a caller-supplied buffer. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Caller fully manages the buffer.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON tree.
buffer must point to writable memory of at least length bytes; must not be NULL.
length must be sufficient; due to estimation inaccuracy, allocate at least 5 extra bytes than strictly needed (per note).
format==0 for unformatted, non-zero for formatted output.
On failure, buffer content is unspecified; no allocation occurs.

functions.name: cJSON_Delete
functions.description: Recursively frees a cJSON item and all of its children, respecting reference flags.
requirements: item may be NULL (no effect).
Pointer must have been obtained from cJSON creation or parse APIs (not stack/static).
After call, item and all detached children become invalid.

functions.name: cJSON_GetArraySize
functions.description: Returns the number of items in a cJSON array or object.
requirements: array must be a valid cJSON pointer; non-array/object may return 0.
Does not modify the input.

functions.name: cJSON_GetArrayItem
functions.description: Returns the item at the given index in a cJSON array, or NULL on failure/out of range.
requirements: array should be a cJSON array.
index is zero-based and must be within bounds [0, size-1] to succeed.
Returned pointer is owned by the array; do not free it; valid while array exists.

functions.name: cJSON_GetObjectItem
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_GetObjectItem(const cJSON * const object, const char * const string)
functions.description: Retrieves the value for a key from a cJSON object, case-insensitive. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: object should be a cJSON object.
string must be a NUL-terminated key name; must not be NULL.
Returned pointer is owned by object; do not free it.

functions.name: cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive(const cJSON * const object, const char * const string)
functions.description: Retrieves the value for a key from a cJSON object, case-sensitive. Returns NULL if not found.
requirements: object should be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
Return is owned by object; do not free.

functions.name: cJSON_HasObjectItem
functions.description: Checks whether a cJSON object contains a key (case-sensitive or insensitive depends on implementation; header implies a check). Returns 1 if present, 0 otherwise.
requirements: object should be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_GetErrorPtr
functions.description: On parse failure, returns a pointer into the input where the error occurred; otherwise returns 0/null when the last parse succeeded.
requirements: Meaningful only after a parse function returns NULL.
Returned pointer points into the original input buffer; do not free or use after the input buffer’s lifetime ends.

functions.name: cJSON_GetStringValue
functions.description: If item is a string, returns its internal valuestring; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by item; do not free or modify.
Only meaningful when cJSON_IsString(item) is true.

functions.name: cJSON_GetNumberValue
functions.description: If item is a number, returns its numeric value; otherwise returns 0 (per typical cJSON behavior).
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Callers should verify type with cJSON_IsNumber for strict handling.

functions.name: cJSON_IsInvalid
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is invalid (type cJSON_Invalid), else 0.
requirements: item may be NULL; NULL or invalid yields 1 per comparison semantics in library (unknown exact NULL handling for this predicate; treat NULL as not a valid item).

functions.name: cJSON_IsFalse
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON false, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsTrue
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON true, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsBool
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON boolean (true or false), else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsNull
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON null, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsNumber
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON number, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsString
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON string, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsArray
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON array, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsObject
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is a JSON object, else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_IsRaw
functions.description: Returns 1 if the item is raw JSON (cJSON_Raw), else 0.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer or NULL.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateNull
functions.description: Creates a cJSON null value node.
requirements: Returns a heap-allocated cJSON* or NULL on allocation failure.
Caller must free with cJSON_Delete or attach to a parent that will be deleted later.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateTrue
functions.description: Creates a cJSON boolean true node.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateFalse
functions.description: Creates a cJSON boolean false node.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateBool
functions.description: Creates a cJSON boolean node set to the given value.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateNumber
functions.description: Creates a cJSON number node with the specified value.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateString
functions.description: Creates a cJSON string node by copying the provided C string.
requirements: string must be NUL-terminated and non-NULL.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateRaw
functions.description: Creates a cJSON raw node containing literal JSON text (embedded raw JSON).
requirements: raw must be a NUL-terminated string containing JSON; not validated beyond storage at creation time.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateArray
functions.description: Creates an empty cJSON array node.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateObject
functions.description: Creates an empty cJSON object node.
requirements: Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateStringReference
functions.description: Creates a cJSON string node that references the provided string memory without copying it; cJSON_Delete will not free the referenced string.
requirements: string must remain valid for the lifetime of the cJSON node.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateObjectReference
functions.description: Creates an object node that references its elements (does not take ownership), so deleting the reference will not free the referenced children.
requirements: child should be a cJSON object to be referenced.
Referenced elements must outlive the reference node.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateArrayReference
functions.description: Creates an array node that references its elements without taking ownership.
requirements: child should be a cJSON array to be referenced.
Referenced elements must outlive the reference node.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateIntArray
functions.description: Creates a cJSON array filled with count integers copied from numbers.
requirements: numbers must point to an array of at least count ints; must not be NULL when count>0.
count must be >= 0.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure; free with cJSON_Delete if not attached.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateFloatArray
functions.description: Creates a cJSON array filled with count floats copied from numbers.
requirements: numbers must point to at least count floats (if count>0).
count must be >= 0.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateDoubleArray
functions.description: Creates a cJSON array filled with count doubles copied from numbers.
requirements: numbers must point to at least count doubles (if count>0).
count must be >= 0.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_CreateStringArray
functions.description: Creates a cJSON array of strings (each element is copied) from an array of C strings.
requirements: strings must point to at least count pointers; each strings[i] must be a NUL-terminated C string when count>0.
count must be >= 0.
Returns allocated node or NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_AddItemToArray
functions.description: Appends item to the end of array.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
item must be a detached cJSON node (not currently linked elsewhere) or a reference intended to be linked.
On success, ownership transfers to array; do not free item directly afterwards.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_AddItemToObject
functions.description: Adds a named item to an object, copying the key string.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated key; must not be NULL.
item must be a cJSON node not already linked elsewhere (unless adding a reference).
On success, object owns item; do not free item directly.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS
functions.description: Adds a named item to an object using the key string as a const reference (no copy).
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must remain valid for the lifetime of the object or until the key is replaced.
WARNING: Before writing to item->string later, check that (item->type & cJSON_StringIsConst) == 0, as per header comment.
item is owned by object on success.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray
functions.description: Appends a reference to item into array; useful for sharing nodes without duplicating content.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
item must be a valid cJSON pointer; reference semantics mean original item must outlive the array entry referencing it.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject
functions.description: Adds a named reference to item into object; object does not own the referenced value’s memory.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
item must remain valid for the lifetime of its reference in object.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer
functions.description: Detaches item from its parent without deleting it and returns the detached item.
requirements: parent must be the current parent of item.
item must be a child of parent.
Caller becomes responsible for the returned item (free with cJSON_Delete or reattach).
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_DetachItemFromArray
functions.description: Detaches and returns the element at index which from array without deleting it.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
which must be within [0, size-1] for success.
Caller owns the returned item; free with cJSON_Delete or reattach.

functions.name: cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray
functions.description: Deletes the element at index which from array.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
which must be within [0, size-1].
After deletion, the removed element is freed and invalid.

functions.name: cJSON_DetachItemFromObject
functions.description: Detaches and returns the member with the given key from object (case-insensitive).
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated key.
Returned item is owned by caller and must be freed or reattached.

functions.name: cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive
functions.description: Detaches and returns the member with the given key from object (case-sensitive).
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
Caller owns returned item.

functions.name: cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject
functions.description: Deletes the member with the given key from object (case-insensitive).
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
After return the removed item is freed and invalid.

functions.name: cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive
functions.description: Deletes the member with the given key from object (case-sensitive).
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_InsertItemInArray
functions.description: Inserts newitem at index which in array, shifting existing items to the right.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
which must be within [0, size] (insertion at size appends).
newitem must be detached or a reference; upon success, array owns newitem.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer
functions.signature: cJSON_bool cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer(cJSON * const parent, cJSON * const item, cJSON * replacement)
functions.description: Replaces item within its parent by replacement using a direct pointer, preserving position, then deletes the old item appropriately.
requirements: parent must be the current parent of item.
item must be a child of parent.
replacement must be a valid cJSON node (detached or reference).
On success, parent owns replacement; returns 1. Returns 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray
functions.description: Replaces the array element at index which with newitem.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array.
which must be within [0, size-1].
newitem must be a valid cJSON node; on success array owns it.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject
functions.description: Replaces the member with the given key (case-insensitive) with newitem; adds if not present in some implementations.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
newitem must be valid; on success object owns it.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive
functions.description: Replaces the member with the given key (case-sensitive) with newitem.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
On success, object owns newitem; returns 1, else 0.

functions.name: cJSON_Duplicate
functions.description: Duplicates a cJSON item. If recurse is non-zero, duplicates the entire subtree. next/prev pointers are cleared in the duplicate.
requirements: item must be a valid cJSON pointer.
Returns a newly allocated cJSON* or NULL on failure; caller must free with cJSON_Delete.
If recurse==0, only the single node is duplicated without its children.

functions.name: cJSON_Compare
functions.signature: cJSON_bool cJSON_Compare(const cJSON * const a, const cJSON * const b, const cJSON_bool case_sensitive)
functions.description: Recursively compares two cJSON trees for equality. If either input is NULL or invalid, they are considered unequal.
requirements: a and b should be valid cJSON pointers.
case_sensitive non-zero enforces case-sensitive key comparison for objects.
Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise; does not modify inputs.

functions.name: cJSON_Minify
functions.description: In-place minifier that removes whitespace characters (' ', '\t', '\r', '\n') from a JSON string buffer.
requirements: json must point to a readable and writable buffer (not a string literal/read-only storage).
Buffer must be NUL-terminated.
Operation is destructive to formatting; use only when modification is acceptable.

functions.name: cJSON_AddNullToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddNullToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)
functions.description: Creates a null node and adds it to object under name. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated key.
On success, object owns the returned node; do not free separately.

functions.name: cJSON_AddTrueToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddTrueToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)
functions.description: Creates a true node and adds it to object under name. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddFalseToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddFalseToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)
functions.description: Creates a false node and adds it to object under name. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddBoolToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddBoolToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name, const cJSON_bool boolean)
functions.description: Creates a boolean node set to boolean and adds it to object. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddNumberToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddNumberToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name, const double number)
functions.description: Creates a number node set to number and adds it to object. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddStringToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddStringToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name, const char * const string)
functions.description: Creates a string node (copying content) and adds it to object under name. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name and string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddRawToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddRawToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name, const char * const raw)
functions.description: Creates a raw JSON node containing raw and adds it to object. Returns the added item or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name and raw must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
raw should contain valid JSON when later printed/used.

functions.name: cJSON_AddObjectToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddObjectToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)
functions.description: Creates an empty object node and adds it under name. Returns the added object or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_AddArrayToObject
functions.signature: cJSON* cJSON_AddArrayToObject(cJSON * const object, const char * const name)
functions.description: Creates an empty array node and adds it under name. Returns the added array or NULL on failure.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object.
name must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.

functions.name: cJSON_SetNumberHelper
functions.description: Helper used by the cJSON_SetNumberValue macro to set a number node's value (updates both valueint and valuedouble internally).
requirements: object must be a valid cJSON number node.
Returns the set value as double; does not allocate.

functions.name: cJSON_SetValuestring
functions.description: Replaces the valuestring of a cJSON string node. Only has effect if object's type is cJSON_String.
requirements: object must be a cJSON string node; otherwise does nothing and returns possibly NULL (per comment: only takes effect when type is cJSON_String).
valuestring must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated C string.
Returned pointer is the internal valuestring; owned by object.

functions.name: cJSON_malloc
functions.description: Allocates memory using the malloc hook set via cJSON_InitHooks, or standard malloc if none set.
requirements: size may be 0 (implementation-defined behavior).
Caller must free with cJSON_free (or the configured free function).

functions.name: cJSON_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by cJSON_malloc/printing functions using the configured free hook or standard free.
requirements: object may be NULL (no effect).
Pointer must have been allocated with the corresponding allocator.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_GetPointer
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_GetPointer(cJSON * const object, const char *pointer)
functions.description: Resolves an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer against object (case-insensitive key matching). Returns the addressed node or NULL.
requirements: object must be a cJSON object/array tree root.
pointer must be a valid NUL-terminated JSON Pointer string (starting with '/' or empty for the root).
Returned node is owned by object; do not free.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_GetPointerCaseSensitive
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_GetPointerCaseSensitive(cJSON * const object, const char *pointer)
functions.description: Resolves an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer against object with case-sensitive key matching. Returns the addressed node or NULL.
requirements: object must be a valid cJSON tree.
pointer must be a NUL-terminated JSON Pointer string.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_GeneratePatches
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_GeneratePatches(cJSON * const from, cJSON * const to)
functions.description: Generates an RFC 6902 JSON Patch array transforming from into to (case-insensitive for keys). Note: modifies from and to by sorting object members by key.
requirements: from and to must be valid cJSON trees.
Callers must not rely on original key order of from/to after call (they are sorted).
Returns a newly allocated cJSON array of patch operations or NULL on failure; caller must free with cJSON_Delete.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_GeneratePatchesCaseSensitive
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_GeneratePatchesCaseSensitive(cJSON * const from, cJSON * const to)
functions.description: Like cJSONUtils_GeneratePatches but treats object keys case-sensitively. Also sorts members of from/to by key.
requirements: from and to must be valid cJSON trees.
Returns a new patch array (caller must free) or NULL on failure.
from and to are modified (sorted).

functions.name: cJSONUtils_AddPatchToArray
functions.signature: void cJSONUtils_AddPatchToArray(cJSON * const array, const char * const operation, const char * const path, const cJSON * const value)
functions.description: Utility to append a single RFC 6902 patch operation object to an existing patch array.
requirements: array must be a cJSON array intended to hold patch operations.
operation must be one of the JSON Patch operations (e.g., "add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", "test"); string must be non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
path must be a valid JSON Pointer path string; non-NULL and NUL-terminated.
value may be NULL for operations that do not require it (implementation follows RFC semantics).
array is modified in-place.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches
functions.signature: int cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches(cJSON * const object, const cJSON * const patches)
functions.description: Applies an RFC 6902 JSON Patch array to object. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure. Not atomic on failure.
requirements: object must be a modifiable cJSON tree root.
patches must be a cJSON array of patch operations.
On failure, object may be left partially modified (non-atomic).
Return value 0 indicates success.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_ApplyPatchesCaseSensitive
functions.signature: int cJSONUtils_ApplyPatchesCaseSensitive(cJSON * const object, const cJSON * const patches)
functions.description: Applies a JSON Patch array with case-sensitive key matching. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure; not atomic on failure.
requirements: object must be a modifiable cJSON tree.
patches must be a cJSON array of operations.
Object may be partially modified on error.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_MergePatch
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_MergePatch(cJSON *target, const cJSON * const patch)
functions.description: Applies an RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch to target. Modifies and returns the (possibly new) target pointer.
requirements: target must be a cJSON value to be patched; may be replaced by a new tree.
patch must be a valid cJSON value representing the merge patch document.
Returned pointer is the new target; caller is responsible for managing its lifetime (free with cJSON_Delete when done).

functions.name: cJSONUtils_MergePatchCaseSensitive
functions.signature: cJSON * cJSONUtils_MergePatchCaseSensitive(cJSON *target, const cJSON * const patch)
functions.description: Like cJSONUtils_MergePatch but treats object keys case-sensitively.
requirements: target and patch as above.
Returns possibly new target pointer; manage lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: cJSONUtils_GenerateMergePatch

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid JSON object keys (C NUL-terminated strings at consumer side).
# These keys should exercise different code paths: empty/non-empty handling, case sensitivity,
# Unicode, escape sequences (as source bytes, not JSON-escaped), long/short, repeated keys, etc.
# The fuzz stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain keys and other strings. Our single buffer will
# contain a sequence of NUL-terminated strings so the harness can slice them as independent params.
# We therefore emit multiple keys and ancillary strings in one buffer, separated by '\0'.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"

# Some interesting Unicode codepoints (UTF-8 encoded).
UNICODE_POINTS = [
    0x00A9,  # ©
    0x03B1,  # α
    0x0416,  # Ж
    0x4F60,  # 你
    0x597D,  # 好
    0x20AC,  # €
    0x1F600, # 😀
    0x00E9,  # é
]

def rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(n))

def rand_unicode(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = []
    for _ in range(n):
        cp = r.choice(UNICODE_POINTS)
        s.append(chr(cp))
    # Mix in ASCII sometimes
    if n > 0 and r.random() < 0.5:
        idx = r.randrange(n)
        s[idx] = r.choice(ASCII_SAFE)
    return ''.join(s)

def rand_numeric_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Keys that look like numbers to differentiate from array indices in JSON Pointer code paths.
    choices = [
        lambda: str(r.randint(0, 1_000_000)),
        lambda: f"-{r.randint(1, 1_000_000)}",
        lambda: f"{r.randint(0,999)}.{r.randint(0,999)}",
        lambda: f"0{r.randint(0,999)}",
    ]
    return r.choice(choices)()

def rand_specials(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include characters that are legal in JSON strings but interesting for key comparisons.
    # Note: We output raw bytes; the library will treat them as C strings and escape on print.
    specials = [
        'Key With Spaces',
        'tabs\tinside',
        'line\nbreak',
        'quote"double',
        "quote'single",
        'slash/forward',
        'back\\slash',
        'colon:semi;comma,',
        'braces{}[]',
        'at@hash#dollar$percent%caret^',
    ]
    return r.choice(specials)

def interesting_keys(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    keys: List[str] = []
    # Include empty and minimal keys first (stubs sometimes replace empty with default).
    keys.append("")
    keys.append("k")
    keys.append("K")  # case-sensitive checks
    keys.append("key")
    keys.append("Key")
    keys.append("KEY")
    # numeric-like
    keys.append(rand_numeric_like(r))
    keys.append(rand_numeric_like(r))
    # ASCII random of varying lengths
    keys.append(rand_ascii(r, 2, 8))
    keys.append(rand_ascii(r, 9, 16))
    # Unicode keys
    keys.append(rand_unicode(r, 1, 4))
    keys.append(rand_unicode(r, 5, 10))
    # Specials / escaped-interesting
    keys.append(rand_specials(r))
    # Very long key (within limits)
    long_len = r.randint(64, 256)
    keys.append(rand_ascii(r, long_len, long_len))
    # Potential duplicates for replacement paths
    base = rand_ascii(r, 3, 6)
    keys.append(base)
    keys.append(base.lower())
    keys.append(base.upper())
    return keys

def ancillary_values(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Values for CreateString/AddRaw, etc.
    vals: List[str] = []
    vals.append("value")
    vals.append(rand_ascii(r, 1, 20))
    vals.append(rand_unicode(r, 1, 8))
    # Raw JSON snippets that are valid when embedded as raw nodes
    raws = [
        'null',
        'true',
        'false',
        '123',
        '3.14159',
        '"raw string"',
        '{"a":1,"b":[1,2,3]}',
        '[{"x":1},{"y":2}]',
    ]
    vals.extend(r.choice(raws) for _ in range(2))
    return vals

def pack_c_strings(parts: List[str], limit: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for s in parts:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        if len(out) + len(b) + 1 > limit:
            break
        out += b + b"\x00"
    # Ensure at least one terminator
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Compose sequence prioritizing keys because multiple stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for keys.
    keys = interesting_keys(r)
    # Shuffle to vary placement per seed but keep deterministic for a given seed.
    r.shuffle(keys)
    parts.extend(keys)

    # Add ancillary strings used for values/raw payloads in add/replace stubs.
    vals = ancillary_values(r)
    r.shuffle(vals)
    parts.extend(vals)

    # Add a few extra random keys to increase diversity.
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.4:
            parts.append(rand_ascii(r, 1, 12))
        elif choice < 0.7:
            parts.append(rand_unicode(r, 1, 6))
        else:
            parts.append(rand_specials(r))

    # Pack into NUL-terminated sequence within 4096 bytes.
    return pack_c_strings(parts, MAX_TOTAL)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets cJSON stubs that consume NUL-terminated strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We produce a single bytes buffer that the harness will slice for each FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME call.
# Goals:
# - Provide valid C strings (contain a terminating NUL) with diverse content to exercise:
#   * Regular UTF-8 text
#   * Empty strings
#   * Very long strings (but <= 4096 total)
#   * Strings that look like JSON, numbers, booleans, null
#   * Strings with escape sequences and control chars
#   * Keys commonly used in object operations (stable literal for CS variant)
# - Include multiple strings back-to-back separated by NUL to serve multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINT) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte UTF-8 ranges
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.75:
            out.append(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINT))
        elif t < 0.90:
            # Latin-1 supplement
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x00FF)))
        elif t < 0.97:
            # Greek/Cyrillic
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x0370, 0x052F)))
        else:
            # Emoji block subset
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x1F300, 0x1F64F)))
    return ''.join(out)


def _json_like_samples(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Samples tailored for the stubs that create strings, add strings/raw to objects, and array operations
    small_nums = ["0", "1", "-1", "3.14159", "-0.0", "1e10", "-2.5e-3"]
    bools = ["true", "false"]
    nulls = ["null"]
    # Various JSON string payloads (as plain strings; for CreateString they are just C-strings)
    str_payloads = [
        "",  # empty allowed and useful for name fixups
        "simple",
        "with spaces",
        "newline\ninside",
        "tab\tinside",
        "quote \" inside",
        "backslash \\",
        "unicode snowman ☃",
    ]
    # Raw JSON objects/arrays to exercise AddRawToObject and potential later prints
    objs = [
        "{}",
        "[]",
        '{"a":1}',
        '{"key": "value"}',
        '{"nested": {"x": [1,2,3], "y": true}}',
        '{"Null": null, "Bool": false, "Num": -12.34}',
    ]
    arrays = [
        "[1,2,3]",
        '["a","b","c"]',
        "[true,false,null,0,1,-2,3.14]",
    ]
    # Keys commonly used; include literal used by CS variant
    keys = [
        "k",
        "key",
        "name",
        "id",
        "key_cs_literal",  # used by cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS
        "α",
        "emoji_😀",
    ]
    # Mix in longer texts
    long_txt = _rand_utf8(rng, rng.randint(64, 256))
    long_ascii = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(64, 256))

    samples = []
    samples.extend(keys)
    samples.extend(str_payloads)
    samples.extend(objs)
    samples.extend(arrays)
    samples.extend(bools)
    samples.extend(nulls)
    samples.extend(small_nums)
    samples.append(long_txt)
    samples.append(long_ascii)

    # Add a couple of randomized JSON-like objects with random keys/values
    for _ in range(3):
        k1 = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 6))
        k2 = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 6))
        v1 = rng.choice(small_nums + bools + nulls)
        v2 = '"' + _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 8)).replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
        samples.append('{"%s": %s, "%s": %s}' % (k1, v1, k2, v2))

    return samples


def _build_buffer(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL terminators; ensure final NUL at end
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b"\x00"
        if total + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)
    # Guarantee at least one empty string if nothing fit
    if not parts:
        parts = [b"\x00"]
    # Ensure overall size <= MAX_TOTAL
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # ensure last byte is NUL to avoid truncating a string without terminator
        data = data[:-1] + b"\x00"
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Include an empty string early for cases where stubs replace empties with defaults
    strings.append("")

    # Deterministic base samples
    strings.extend(_json_like_samples(rng))

    # Add a couple of filenames-looking entries for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers (if any appear)
    filenames = [
        "input.json",
        "data.txt",
        "复杂/路径/файл.json",
        "C:\\path\\to\\file.json",
    ]
    strings.extend(filenames)

    # Add variants of keys and values commonly used in object/array edits
    for _ in range(5):
        strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 12)))
        strings.append(_rand_utf8(rng, rng.randint(1, 12)))

    # Add some longer JSON arrays/objects to exercise insertion/replacement after parsing or raw storage
    for _ in range(2):
        arr = '[' + ','.join(str(rng.randint(-5, 5)) for __ in range(rng.randint(5, 15))) + ']'
        strings.append(arr)
    for _ in range(2):
        kvs = []
        for __ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            k = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 8))
            v_kind = rng.randint(0, 3)
            if v_kind == 0:
                v = '"' + _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 10)).replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
            elif v_kind == 1:
                v = str(rng.uniform(-1000, 1000))
            elif v_kind == 2:
                v = rng.choice(["true", "false", "null"])
            else:
                v = '[' + ','.join(str(rng.randint(0, 3)) for ___ in range(rng.randint(0, 5))) + ']'
            kvs.append('"%s":%s' % (k, v))
        strings.append('{' + ','.join(kvs) + '}')

    # Ensure presence of the exact key used by CS add
    strings.append("key_cs_literal")

    # Add boundary-length strings near the size limit but still valid when NUL-terminated
    # Compute remaining capacity to decide lengths
    prelim = _build_buffer(strings)
    remaining = MAX_TOTAL - len(prelim)
    if remaining > 16:
        big_len = min(remaining - 1, 512)
        strings.append(_rand_utf8(rng, big_len // 2))
        strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, min(remaining // 2, 512)))

    return _build_buffer(strings)
